transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-01
Time: 08:00 AM PT / 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Moore (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Jamal Ortiz (Redwood), Sarah Lin (AcuteHealth Head of ML), Carlos Vega (SRE), Maya Thompson (Security), Ravi Patel (Platform)

Summary (auto): Weekly POC sync for Redwood Private VPC pilot. Reviewed current networking blockers (peering, NATs), security doc gaps, and performance tuning tasks (KV-cache tests). Agreed on deadlines for network diagram and tuning results; tentative on-prem install week discussed.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh, quick check — everyone see calendar and good to go?
[00:08] Sarah: Yep, looks good, thanks Ethan.
[00:10] Priya: Morning all, I'll drive the tech bits — want to kick off with the network status?
[00:15] Carlos: Sure, quick update from our side: we put together the initial peering request yesterday but ran into an IP overlap with one of our legacy VPCs, so we need to confirm the CIDR ranges.
[00:27] Ethan: Okay, good call out. Carlos can you put the CIDR list into the shared doc, and also note whether you want a static NAT or a NAT gateway? That will affect the egress config on Redwood Private side.
[00:40] Carlos: Yep, I'll put that in. Quick question — for the on-prem option, do you require a bastion host for the install, or can we use an existing jumphost?
[00:48] Priya: We can work with either. For security we're partial to a dedicated bastion or SSM session manager, mainly so we can lock down ports during install. If you have an existing hardened jumphost, we can use it but we'll need IP allowlist details.
[01:05] Maya: From security: we need RBAC mapping and SSO integration details before we sign off. Also, audit-log retention — what's Redwood's default?
[01:13] Ethan: Good question. Our platform captures audit logs to the customer's KMS-backed bucket — retention is configurable; default is 90 days but we can do longer for enterprise plans. We'll send the SOC2/ISO docs and the KMS/HSM integration guide after this meeting.
[01:30] Sarah: Awesome. One more — latency targets. We ran the sample baseline yesterday and saw 180-220ms p95 on hosted; what's realistic on the Private pilot?
[01:40] Priya: On the Private side, with the current 4xA100 config and KV-cache, we should aim for p95 in the 120-160ms ballpark for gen tasks at 1k context. That said, it depends on batching and whether prefix caching hits are high. We're running a KV-cache tuning pass this week.
[02:00] Carlos: Sorry, quick dumb question — when you say "KV cache" do you mean the prefix cache or the key-value cache in the model runtime?
[02:07] Priya: Yeah, bad phrasing — I mean the runtime KV cache, the key-value caching of past tokens. Sometimes people call it prefix cache, kay-vee cash, whatever — it's the same thing. The cache hit rate matters a lot.
[02:20] Sarah: Got it. And batching — any recommended batch sizes for low latency?
[02:24] Priya: For this workload we've seen diminishing returns beyond batch sizes of 8-16 for single-request latency. If you're doing throughput-heavy reranking, larger batches help cost, but latency suffers. We'll share the tuning sheet.
[02:40] Ethan: Quick note — customer asked about quantization on-prem. We do support 4-bit quant on compatible models, but we need to validate accuracy regressions for your eval set. That's a separate task.
[02:52] Sarah: Yes please, we want to see quality numbers. Can you run a 1000-prompt eval with 4-bit vs fp16?
[02:58] Priya: We can. It might take 2-3 days to run, but we'll prioritize output-quality comparisons and share the evaluation spreadsheet.
[03:10] Jamal: (note) referenced bench spreadsheet link: https://redwood.app/bench/acutehealth-pilot (shared in chat)
[03:18] Carlos: On routing — we prefer egress through our NATs for compliance reasons. Is there an easy way to force egress via our gateway?
[03:25] Priya: Yes, we can route egress through your NAT gateway via VPC peering and specific route tables. For higher control we also support running in a private subnet with no public egress and a customer-managed NAT. We'll include a proposed route table diagram.
[03:42] Maya: Regarding keys — do you support customer-managed KMS? We can't have Redwood hold plaintext keys.
[03:48] Ethan: Absolutely. We support customer KMS/HSM integrations; keys are used only for envelopes and we log decryption events. We'll send the KMS/HSM integration doc and the exact API calls that will appear in audit logs.
[04:05] Sarah: Perfect. Any blockers on our side to get peering done quickly?
[04:09] Carlos: Biggest blocker is CIDR overlap and getting firewall team signoff. Also need a tentative maintenance window for the on-prem install — we prefer weekends.
[04:20] Ethan: Weekend install is fine. We suggested week of 2026-04-13 as tentative; if weekends work better we can aim for 2026-04-18.
[04:30] Ravi: We're also tracking compliance review — internal legal wants to see SOC2 + encryption details before infra approvals.
[04:36] Ethan: We'll attach the SOC2 report and encryption guide.
[04:40] Priya: Switching gears — perf tuning updates. I ran a short KV-cache experiment last night. Baseline: cold cache p95 was ~400ms, warm cache p95 dropped to ~140ms. With a conservative batching policy we can keep p95 ~150ms and lower tokens cost by ~22%.
[04:58] Sarah: That's promising. Did you use continuous batching or fixed time-window batching?
[05:02] Priya: Continuous batching with adaptive windowing based on arrival rates. There's a config param "max_latency_ms" that you can tune — raising it to 40ms gave better batching but added tail latency.
[05:18] Carlos: For our user flows the majority of calls are short chat completions — tail latency matters more. We prefer slightly lower batching to protect p95.
[05:25] Priya: Totally understood — we can give two config recommendations: p95-optimized and cost-optimized.
[05:31] Sarah: Great. Can you share the config diffs in the sheet?
[05:34] Priya: Yep, will upload.
[05:36] Ethan: Any procurement/legal asks?
[05:38] Maya: Our procurement wants the standard terms redline. Also need to confirm data residency and whether logs can be forwarded to our SIEM.
[05:46] Ethan: Logs can be forwarded; we'll include SIEM syslog integration notes and the fields included in audit logs. We'll also note residence options — region choice for the private control plane and where persistent data is stored.
[05:59] Sarah: One more technical — when you do model rollouts, what's the canary behavior in Private? We want to avoid degradations mid-run.
[06:06] Priya: In Private we support canary percentages and automatic rollback on error thresholds. For long-running requests we drain connections and use graceful fallback to a stable variant. We'll share the rollout doc.
[06:20] Carlos: Nice. On upgrades — do you require a specific downtime window?
[06:25] Priya: Upgrades are zero-downtime for the serving runtime usually but control-plane upgrades can be scheduled; we'll provide a recommended maintenance window. For critical upgrades we coordinate with your SRE.
[06:37] Sarah: Sounds good. For the quant eval and KV-cache tuning — can we get the numbers before next sync?
[06:43] Priya: We'll try; KV-cache tuning should be ready by 2026-04-08, quant eval maybe by 2026-04-06 depending on queue.
[06:52] Ethan: Okay let's capture next steps.
[07:00] (Several attendees briefly talk over each other)
[07:05] Ethan: Recap: Redwood sends SOC2 + KMS docs, network diagram with NAT/bastion proposal by 2026-04-03; AcuteHealth provides CIDR ranges and peering details by 2026-04-05; Priya runs KV-cache tuning and shares perf sheet by 2026-04-08; schedule tentative on-prem install week of 2026-04-13. Any objections?
[07:25] Sarah: No objections.
[07:27] Carlos: All good.
[07:30] Maya: We'll review SOC2 and come back if anything missing.
[07:34] Ethan: Great. We'll follow up in chat with links. Thanks everyone.
[07:40] Sarah: Thanks all.

End of transcript.

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts ("kay-vee cash"), speakers sometimes overlapped; shared artifacts: bench spreadsheet link (https://redwood.app/bench/acutehealth-pilot), preliminary network diagram (attached in chat).
